:::{#thm-moore-penrose-gram}
#### The Moore-Penrose inverse of a Gram matrix

For every $m \times n$ [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) $\matr{A}$,

$$
(\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{A})^+ = \matr{A}^+\,\tp{(\matr{A}^+)}.
$$

:::

::: proof

Let $\matr{M} = \tp{\matr{A}}\matr{A}$ and $\matr{G} = \matr{A}^+\,\tp{(\matr{A}^+)}$.
By @thm-moore-penrose-unique, it is enough to show that $\matr{G}$ satisfies the four conditions of @def-moore-penrose for $\matr{M}$.

**Two identities.**
Conditions 3 and 4 for $\matr{A}^+$ say that $\matr{A}\matr{A}^+$ and $\matr{A}^+\matr{A}$ are [symmetric](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix).
Using condition 1 for $\matr{A}^+$,

$$
\ba
\tp{\matr{A}}\,\matr{A}\matr{A}^+
&= \tp{\matr{A}}\,\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{A}^+)}
&& \text{(condition 3 for } \matr{A}^+ \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{(\matr{A}\matr{A}^+\matr{A})}
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}}.
&& \text{(condition 1 for } \matr{A}^+ \text{)}
\ea
$$

So

$$
\ba
\matr{M}\matr{G}
&= \tp{\matr{A}}\,\matr{A}\matr{A}^+\,\tp{(\matr{A}^+)}
&& \text{(definitions of } \matr{M} \text{ and } \matr{G} \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}}\,\tp{(\matr{A}^+)}
&& (\tp{\matr{A}}\,\matr{A}\matr{A}^+ = \tp{\matr{A}})
\\
&= \tp{(\matr{A}^+\matr{A})},
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\ea
$$

which is $\matr{A}^+\matr{A}$ by condition 4 for $\matr{A}^+$.
Hence $\matr{M}\matr{G} = \matr{A}^+\matr{A}$,
and it is symmetric,
which is condition 3 for $\matr{G}$.

For the other order,

$$
\ba
\matr{G}\matr{M}
&= \matr{A}^+\,\tp{(\matr{A}^+)}\,\tp{\matr{A}}\,\matr{A}
&& \text{(definitions of } \matr{G} \text{ and } \matr{M} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{A}^+\,\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{A}^+)}\,\matr{A}
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\\
&= \matr{A}^+\matr{A}\matr{A}^+\matr{A}
&& \text{(condition 3 for } \matr{A}^+ \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{A}^+\matr{A},
&& \text{(condition 1 for } \matr{A}^+ \text{)}
\ea
$$

so $\matr{G}\matr{M} = \matr{A}^+\matr{A}$ is symmetric,
which is condition 4 for $\matr{G}$.

**Conditions 1 and 2.**

$$
\ba
\matr{M}\matr{G}\matr{M}
&= \matr{A}^+\matr{A}\,\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{A}
&& (\matr{M}\matr{G} = \matr{A}^+\matr{A})
\\
&= \tp{(\matr{A}^+\matr{A})}\,\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{A}
&& \text{(condition 4 for } \matr{A}^+ \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{(\matr{A}\matr{A}^+\matr{A})}\,\matr{A}
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}}\matr{A}
&& \text{(condition 1 for } \matr{A}^+ \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{M},
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{M} \text{)}
\\
\matr{G}\matr{M}\matr{G}
&= \matr{A}^+\matr{A}\,\matr{A}^+\,\tp{(\matr{A}^+)}
&& (\matr{G}\matr{M} = \matr{A}^+\matr{A})
\\
&= \matr{A}^+\,\tp{(\matr{A}^+)}
&& \text{(condition 2 for } \matr{A}^+ \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{G}.
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{G} \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
